**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat malformed Gutenberg marker spacing as ambiguous**

When a marker-like line uses unsupported whitespace inside `PROJECT GUTENBERG` (for example, a non-breaking space), `_CANDIDATE.match(value)` succeeds but the literal substring check fails because `_label()` normalizes only spaces and tabs. Consequently, a banner followed by that malformed line and an otherwise valid marker pair is cleaned successfully, deleting the malformed line with the prefix, even though the documented conservative contract says malformed marker-like candidates must preserve the entire input. Detect such candidates without requiring this already-normalized literal phrase so they produce `unrecognized_marker` instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

Single-asterisk Gutenberg delimiters are ignored rather than recorded as malformed. With a Gutenberg banner, damaged single-asterisk outer boundaries, a complete triple-asterisk example inside the narrative, and a license heading, cleanup returns only the example's body and excludes the surrounding narrative. Include single-asterisk delimiters in candidate detection so the existing malformed-marker handling preserves the original. Add an outer-malformed/inner-valid regression.

A supported envelope followed by a second book whose delimiters wrap between `PROJECT` and `GUTENBERG` returns only the first book's body. This gate ignores the wrapped fragments, while the later license heading satisfies the suffix check, so the second book's narrative is excluded from `result.text` with `envelope_removed`. Detect these wrapped fragments as unsupported candidates and preserve the entire input; this should not enable stripping wrapped envelopes. Add a regression combining a supported book with a wrapped one.
